raw_findings.message: The handler reads the entire caller-controlled Content-Length into memory without a limit, so a large request can exhaust server memory.
A missing X-Api-Key becomes the empty string, so callers can upload documents owned by that value and later read them without supplying any credential.
A nonexistent ID makes STORE.get return None, which is dereferenced by can_read and produces HTTP 500 instead of a not-found response.
The purge endpoint checks only whether X-Admin-Key is present, so any caller can supply an arbitrary value and delete every document.
The redirect target is accepted without validation, so an attacker can send users to an arbitrary external site through /go?next=... .
Document titles are interpolated into HTML without escaping, so an uploaded title containing markup executes script for visitors to /docs.html.
Seeding Python's non-cryptographic PRNG with the current time makes share tokens predictable to an attacker who can infer the startup second and observe token issuance.
Share tokens contain only 48 random bits, allowing an attacker to brute-force a valid token, especially because the endpoint has no attempt limit.
Token comparison returns at the first differing character, so repeated measurements can reveal the token prefix.

The in-memory document map starts empty and is never populated from the existing files, so restarting the server makes previously uploaded documents inaccessible and can overwrite their files when IDs are reused.
Concurrent uploads can read the same usage value and all pass this check before any updates it, allowing a caller to exceed the per-key quota.
The staged file is copied but never removed, so every successful upload leaves another payload-sized file in tmp and repeated uploads can exhaust disk space.
An uploader can select object format and provide a pickle payload whose deserialization executes attacker-controlled code.
The supplied URL is opened without scheme or destination restrictions, allowing requests to internal services and reads from local file URLs.
The entire remote response is read into memory before quota enforcement, so a URL serving a very large response can exhaust server memory.
The caller-controlled TTL is not validated, so a negative value creates a share that is expired immediately.
